events.title: The future emperor Nero is born at Antium
events.description: Lucius Domitius Ahenobarbus, later the emperor Nero, was born at Antium to Agrippina the Younger. Adopted by Claudius, he became emperor at 16 and was the last of the Julio-Claudian dynasty.
events.html: Lucius Domitius Ahenobarbus, later the emperor Nero, was born at Antium to Agrippina the Younger. Adopted by Claudius, he became emperor at 16 and was the last of the Julio-Claudian dynasty.

events.title: The Bill of Rights is ratified
events.description: Virginia's approval gave the first ten amendments to the US Constitution the required three-quarters of states. They guarantee freedoms of speech, religion, press and assembly, and rights to due process.
events.html: Virginia's approval gave the first ten amendments to the US Constitution the required three-quarters of states. They guarantee freedoms of speech, religion, press and assembly, and rights to due process.

events.title: Sitting Bull is killed at Standing Rock
events.description: Lakota leader Sitting Bull, a leader at the victory over Custer at the Little Bighorn, was shot dead by Indian police trying to arrest him. Two weeks later came the massacre at Wounded Knee.
events.html: Lakota leader Sitting Bull, a leader at the victory over Custer at the Little Bighorn, was shot dead by Indian police trying to arrest him. Two weeks later came the massacre at Wounded Knee.

events.title: Gone with the Wind premieres in Atlanta
events.description: The film of Margaret Mitchell's novel premiered at Loew's Grand Theatre in Atlanta. It won eight competitive Academy Awards, and allowing for inflation it remains the highest-grossing film ever.
events.html: The film of Margaret Mitchell's novel premiered at Loew's Grand Theatre in Atlanta. It won eight competitive Academy Awards, and allowing for inflation it remains the highest-grossing film ever.

events.title: The Leaning Tower of Pisa reopens
events.description: After eleven years of closure and stabilisation work, the Leaning Tower of Pisa reopened to visitors. Engineers had reduced its tilt by about 44 centimetres, securing it for centuries.
